profile.scope: Separate diagnostic four-second macOS CPU samples of nullable BinaryRowData BIGINT %d, 1024 rows and 32768 loops for initial and actual previous release executables.
profile.observation: Both sampled stacks locate per-row format parsing and integer string allocation/conversion under the formatter. Inclusive counts overlap and cannot be interpreted as wall-time shares. They do not by themselves attribute the regression to a specific branch.
profile.optimization: Compile separate Boolean-capable and integer-only formatting loops; choose once per batch. Reuse the conversion String alongside the row scratch/output builder, and format decimal integers through the existing itoa dependency. Null/Boolean words and hex/octal/character conversions write into this buffer. General certified DECIMAL string conversion keeps its existing owned result without a redundant copy. General certified batches with an equal non-NULL format reuse the same Arrow builder and scratch buffers; variable or NULL formats retain row handling. The intermediate per-conversion ownership experiment did not recover all slower medians and is discarded. It keeps its preceding Boolean-object evaluator; the new Boolean-capable loop is used only after the planner proves its literal primitive contract. Parsing remains rowwise.

limitations: Only Flink 2.2 has PRINTF; released Flink 1.18 rejection is not a native gap.

ASCII literal formats <=512, width/precision <=256, argument-specific conversions and total verified BOOLEAN/integer producers only. Dynamic/non-ASCII formats, other types/conversions and unverified or failing/stateful producers retain existing routes.

Explicit index zero and invalid formats retain the released running JDK behavior through preceding routes. Representation-sensitive consumers keep existing guards.
The initial slower shared formatter, retained old-native controls, independent stock and complete jobs remain recorded; no universal speedup is claimed.
